response.title: which crawl space dehumidifier is the easiest to install yourself
response.answer:
For the easiest DIY installation, I recommend a crawl space dehumidifier that has a built-in condensate pump, a standard 120V plug, and automatic humidity control.

The biggest installation challenge usually isn't operating the dehumidifier. It's getting rid of the water it collects. A built-in pump makes installation much easier because you don't need to position the unit near a floor drain or rely on gravity drainage.

My top choices are ALORAIR, AprilAire, and Santa Fe, but they differ significantly in installation effort.

My top 3 choices for DIY installation
Shop
Easiest overall

AlorAir 198 PPD Crawl Space Dehumidifiers with Pump and Drai…

$1,032.39

Built-in condensate pump, included drain hose, standard 115V power, automatic humidity control. No separate pump installation required.

90 pints/day • 70.5 lb • 17.7 in. tall

View product

Shop

AlorAir Sentinel HDi55

$626.99

Smaller, easier to move into a tight crawl space, with built-in pump drainage. A good option for a smaller area.

55 pints/day class • compact design

View product

Shop

AprilAire E070 70 pt. 2,200 sq. ft. Bucketless Dehumidifier …

$1,769.99

Low-profile unit for tight spaces, with straightforward controls. Best when you already have a gravity drain; otherwise, you'll need a separate pump.

70 pints/day • 12.5 in. tall

View product

The HDi90 is explicitly described by AlorAir as plug-and-play, provided the space is appropriately sealed and drainage is arranged. 
AlorAir
+1

What installation actually involves

For a typical encapsulated crawl space, the work is relatively straightforward:

Put the unit on a stable, level, elevated support.

Connect the condensate discharge hose.

Route the hose to an approved drain or discharge point.

Plug it into a properly grounded outlet.

Set humidity to approximately 50–55% RH.

Test the drainage and verify the unit operates correctly.

You don't normally need HVAC ductwork or hardwiring for a standalone installation. However, adding an electrical outlet, penetrating an exterior wall, or installing a new drain may require professional work.

Two questions that would change my recommendation
How big is your crawl space?
Under 1,000 sq ft
1,000–2,000 sq ft
Over 2,000 sq ft
Where can the collected water drain?
Existing drain lower than the unit
Need to pump water up or outside
Not sure yet
Find my easiest-to-install option

These two details determine whether you can get away with a simple plug-in-and-drain installation or need a more involved setup.
